Date : 20/01/2023  ORAL ORDER Learned Senior Counsel Mr. Unwala is permitted to file his vakalatnama on behalf of the original complainant.

sentences.text: 3.3 In march, 2018, the applicant forced and pressured the complainant to have an unnatural physical relationship with him.
The complainant was not provided any money to spend on her household or personal expenses.
The complainant was allegedly neither allowed to go out of the house alone, nor speak or meet with her parents and relatives.
In December, 2019, the complainant found out that the applicant is having affair with one Manisha Singh, who was an employee of the present applicant .
The applicant also had an affair with his hotel HR manager, Devashri.

In December, 2020, when the complainant was alone at home accused No.3 used to try and get close with the complainant told about the said incident to the applicant and accused No. 2, they beat the complainant, instead of reprimanding the accused No.3.

3.4 The applicant, who is the husband of the complainant, came to be nabbed from Delhi International Airport on 06.01.2023 and R/CR.MA/1372/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 is shown arrested on 07.01.2023.
Thereafter, the remand application preferred by the police through the State, came to be rejected and the applicant was sent to judicial custody on 08.01.2023.

3.5 The applicant, thereafter, had preferred an application for grant of bail, under Section 437 of the Cr.P.C before the Metropolitan Magistrate, Ahmedabad, which came to be rejected vide order dated 09.01.2023.

Thereafter, the applicant on 10.01.2023, preferred an application for grant of bail under Section 439 of the Code before the City Civil & Sessions Court at Ahmedabad, which came to be rejected vide order dated 16.01.2023.

Therefore, the applicant, aggrieved by the said order,
approached this Court for regular bail in connection with the FIR being C.R.No C.R.No.11191030220058 of 2022 with Mahila Police Station (west), Ahmedabad for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 406, 377, 323, 294-B, 506 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code read with section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and has prayed for quashing and setting aside the order dated 10.01.2023 passed by the City Civil & Sessions Court, Ahmedabad passed in Criminal Misc.

R/CR.MA/1372/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 (4) Heard learned advocate Mr. Hriday Buch appearing for the appellant, Mr. Unwala, Senior Counsel for the original complainant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State.

(5) Learned Advocate Mr. Buch appearing for the applicant submits that the complainant has filed the present FIR only with a view to extort monies from the applicant and other accused person and to make the applicant a scapegoat to fraudulently gain on behest of the applicant and his family members.

It is submitted that except the alleged offence under Section 377 of the IPC rest of the offences under Sections 498-A, 406, 323, 294-B, 506 and 114 of the IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, the maximum punishment prescribed is upto 3 years and therefore, considering the variouis pronouncements of the Hon;'ble Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar v State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273.

sentences.text: It is submitted that for proving the offence under Sections 376 and 377 R/CR.MA/1372/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 of IPC, it is necessary to have satisfied the ingredients of Section 375 of the IPC.
Section 375 of the IPC includes within its ambit, any kind of penetration, without the consent and will of the complainant.

However, Section 375 provides for an exception that Sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under fifteen years of age, is not rape and consequently, if section 375 cannot be made out against the present applicant, for any kind of penetration, sexual intercourse of sexual acts with his wife.

It is submitted that as per the FIR, all alleged offences are occurred at Jaipur, China, Hong Kong and USA and not a single offence as alleged is occurred at Ahmedabad even though the FIR is lodged at Ahmedabad though not having jurisdiction which discloses the mal intention of the complainant to falsely arraign the applicant in so called offences.

It is further submitted that applicant is alone in the family and his sister is married and accused in this case and mother is expired succumbed to the CORONA and his father is living on only one kidney and is required to perform dialysis twice a week and there is no other family members in the family to take care and look after his father for such diseases.

It is submitted that complainant- wife has also filed a criminal Misc. Application No.
2212/2022 in R/CR.MA/1372/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 Family Court which is pending for adjudication under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C.

It is submitted that the applicant is having movable and immovable property and is an income tax payer and is a service class person, and therefore, is not likely to abscond or flee from justice, and therefore, the regular bail may be granted to the applicant.
He has placed reliance on the judgment of this Hon'ble Court in the case of Kunal Mahendrabhai Naginlal Patel vs. State of Gujarat passed in Criminal Misc. Application No. 19503 of 2021.

sentences.text: (6) Learned APP appearing for Respondent-State submits that the applicant accused is involved in very serious crime and he does not deserve the bail that there is all likelihood that the presence of accused may not be secured and the applicant-accused likely to tamper with the evidence.
He therefore prayed that looking to the gravity of the offence present applicant may not be enlarged on bail.

(7) From police report, it appears that the marriage of them was done on 29.11.2013 and since then he was beating the complainant and was threatening the complainant for enjoying intercourse and had enjoyed carnal unnatural intercourse with the complainant by force and was not parting money with the complainant for household expenses and was not taking the R/CR.MA/1372/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 complainant out anywhere for loitering and had compelled the complainant to stay along in the house and the other family members of the family were also harassing the complainant and the applicant was time and again pressurizing the complainant for bringing dowry from her parental home.
It further appears that the lookout notice against the present applicant has been issued by the police and he was caught from the Delhi Airport when he was trying to leave India forever.
Further, the complainant-wife has submitted that looking to the passport of the applicant, he is a Chinese Citizen and he will never come back to India, if he run away.

(8) It is observed by the trial Court concerned that unnatural intercourse has been done by the applicant with her and a wife can initiate proceedings against her husband for unnatural sex under Section 377 of IPC.
Section 377 of the IPC does not criminalize a particular class of people or identity or orientation.

R/CR.MA/1372/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 (9) One of the contentions of the learned advocate for the applicant is that F.I.R. was lodged with inordinate delay thus no reliance can be placed and delay in lodging the F.I.R. itself belies the whole prosecution story.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in a catena of judgment has held that mere delay in lodging the FIR is no ground to doubt the prosecution case when it is properly explained.

In case of Tara Singh v. State of Punjab, 1991 Supp (1) SCC 536, reported in AIR 1991 SC 63, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that mere delay in lodging the FIR by itself cannot give scope for an adverse inference leading to rejection of the prosecution case outright.

Moreover, the husband of complainant has constantly tortured the complainant only because of the fact that he has an affair with one Devshree, who was working at HR manager at Jaypur Hotel.

It further transpires from the FIR that that there are no reasonable grounds for believing that the present applicant is not guilty of the alleged offence and that he is R/CR.MA/1372/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 not likely to commit any offence while on bail.

(14) For the foregoing reasons and from the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the prosecution has clearly established the prima facie case against the present applicant and thus, this Court is not inclined to exercise the powers vested under section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure Code for releasing the present applicant on bail before completion of investigation.
